section.title: Before DITA
section.p: A technical writing team at a software company maintains product documentation using Microsoft Word. Each product version requires a separate document. When any common procedure changes, such as the login process, writers must manually update dozens of documents. Inconsistencies creep in. Version control becomes a nightmare. Publishing to the web requires manual conversion, introducing errors.

section.title: After DITA
section.p: The same team adopts DITA. The login procedure becomes a single task topic stored in a shared location. Every document that needs this procedure references it using a content reference (conref). When the login process changes, one update propagates everywhere automatically. Publishing to PDF, HTML, and mobile formats happens from a single source with consistent formatting.
